$comment: The Node runtime shipped inside the desktop application.
One version, pinned by digest, named in exactly one place so the fetch script, the
CI job, the packaging manifest and the documentation cannot disagree.
The digest is the integrity control that matters. Downloading nodejs.org's own
SHASUMS256.txt over TLS proves the file matches what that host is serving today,
which is worth having and is not the same as proving it is the file this
application was built and tested against. A digest committed here is checked
against every download, so a swapped artifact — upstream or in transit through a
proxy — fails the build instead of shipping.
The major version is not free to change. `better-sqlite3` is a native addon and
is loaded by this runtime, so its ABI must match: Node 22 is NODE_MODULE_VERSION
127, and a bundle built against a different major fails at `require` with an
error most users would read as a broken install. The Windows CI job installs this
exact version before `pnpm install` for that reason.
